speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have had these skin lesions and if they are itchy or painful? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) to check for infection.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 12 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual, as those specific skin findings are classic for Molluscum contagiosum, not appendicitis. Did you recently have contact with a child who had similar bumps, or do you have a history of eczema or other skin conditions? REQUEST TEST: Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) to rule out syphilis despite the atypical location.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum. The skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication are pathognomonic for this viral infection, likely spread through close contact. No further tests are needed at this time.
